page: Microsoft Azure D96plds_v7 is an ARM-based virtual machine configuration built on the 64-bit ARM (arm64) architecture and hosted under Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs paired with 192.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes 5670 GB of bundled local NVMe solid-state storage. No graphical processing units (GPUs) are provisioned in this profile.

The Dpldsv7 hardware profile targets high-concurrency computation while constraining memory footprint per core. Because the resource ratio provides 2 GB of RAM per vCPU, the instance yields higher core density relative to memory allocations, delivering qualitative cost advantages for multithreaded jobs that do not require deep memory buffering. The provision of 5670 GB of fast local NVMe storage enables low-latency scratch space and transient data persistence without external network storage overhead. A notable operational tradeoff is the ARM64 ISA requirement, which necessitates ARM-compatible application builds and container images, along with the constrained memory capacity per core compared to standard general-purpose profiles.

Workloads well suited to the D96plds_v7 profile include compute-bound microservices, continuous integration and build compilation pipelines, batch processing, distributed data engineering tasks, video or web asset transcoding, and scale-out web serving fleets that benefit from high thread parallelization and rapid local NVMe caching.
description: Microsoft Azure D96plds_v7 is a compute-focused ARM64 virtual machine featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Designed around a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio yielding 2.0 GB of memory per core, this configuration targets compute-dense processing that does not demand extensive per-thread memory capacity. The instance includes 5670 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage for rapid I/O operations and scratch caching, without discrete GPU hardware acceleration. The combination of dense ARM core allocation and integrated high-capacity local storage provides qualitative cost efficiencies for multithreaded execution, avoiding extra network-attached storage expenditures. Users must ensure binary compatibility with the 64-bit ARM architecture. Recommended workloads comprise distributed batch processing, code compilation clusters, web serving fleets, media transcoding, and data pipelines requiring strong core concurrency coupled with high-capacity local disk operations.
